column1: # groups.tsv -- every highlight group, and which palette role and contrast
# class it belongs to. No colour appears here: only role names from
# palette.toml, which is the only file a colour is typed in.
# Format:  group <TAB> fg <TAB> bg <TAB> sp <TAB> class <TAB> attrs
#   fg/bg/sp   a role name from [ramp] / [ramp_extra] in palette.toml, or
#              "-" for unset, or "none" for an explicitly transparent
#              background (the default background, which is the one kitty
#   class      text | chrome | accent | inverse | fixed. See palette.toml.
#              inverse = dark text on an explicit light background, so the
#              solve moves the BACKGROUND rather than the foreground.
#              A row with no fg but a bg inherits Normal's foreground, and
#              build/check-contrast checks it as fg2 against that background.
#   attrs      bold, italic, underline, undercurl -- comma separated, or "-"
# kitty makes a cell translucent only when its background is the DEFAULT
# background -- verified in kitty 0.48.2's own option documentation: "it only
# sets the background color's opacity in cells that have the same background
# color as the default terminal background". So a group with an explicit bg is
# drawn opaque and is solved against that colour; a group with no bg (or
# bg = none) is solved against T, the composited background.
# nvimrc/init.lua clears the background of twenty groups immediately after
# loading the colourscheme, which is what puts Normal, LineNr, StatusLine and
# the rest into the composited case. The theme is solved to be correct either
# way, so that block neither needs changing nor breaks anything.
# The diff groups carry no foreground, like Visual: in diff mode a foreground
# here replaces the syntax colour, so every added line came out solid pink and
# every changed one solid white. A background alone lets the code keep its
# colours. DiffChange takes the CursorLine shade and DiffText the panel shade,
# so the changed span stands out from its line the way a selection stands out
# from the current line; on dim1 the dim band would sit at 1.85:1. DiffDelete
# keeps its pink: it only paints the filler on the side that has no text.
# build/check-contrast "show-through" measures the syntax colours on these.
